title: Utah doctor speaks out against potential Medicaid cuts in 'Big Beautiful Bill'
text:
Emily Ashcraft is a reporter for KSL.com. She covers issues in state courts, health and religion. In her spare time, Emily enjoys crafting, cycling and raising chickens.
SALT LAKE CITY — A Salt Lake City OB-GYN spoke out in a virtual press conference on Wednesday, along with doctors from three other states whose representatives could make a difference in whether funding is cut from Medicaid.Dr. Addison Alley said the One Big Beautiful Bill that Congress will begin voting on Friday is a "big, dangerous bill" for his patients.
"I don't think I can count the number of times where Medicaid has made a difference in my practice," he said.He talked about multiple women who were able to bring home a healthy baby and whose pregnancy complications were not worsened by a lack of access to care or worry about how they would pay for care."If Congress slashes Medicaid funding, this kind of care disappears for thousands of Utahns," Alley said.
